subject.title: fix(secrets): block prototype-polluting segments in setPathCreateStrict

question: Should OpenClaw accept a shared fail-closed guard that rejects __proto__, constructor, and prototype in setPathCreateStrict for plugin/config writes?
rationale: The patch closes a prototype-pollution boundary in the shared write helper, but it deliberately changes behavior for any existing plugin or config path that used those prototype-like segment names.

options.title: Accept shared fail-closed guard
options.body: Land the central setPathCreateStrict guard and treat those three segment names as invalid across create-strict config writes.

options.title: Add earlier manifest diagnostics
options.body: Ask for an additional manifest/uiHints validation error so plugin authors see the problem before the wizard reaches the shared helper.

options.title: Pause for compatibility evidence
options.body: Hold the PR only if maintainers know of a supported shipped plugin that intentionally uses one of the blocked segment names.

recommendation.title: Accept shared fail-closed guard
recommendation.body: Land the central setPathCreateStrict guard and treat those three segment names as invalid across create-strict config writes.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the shared prototype-key guard and secrets hardening history, making him the best available owner for the security/compatibility tradeoff.
